newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Up to 300 still trapped in Russian Caucasus tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Up to 300 still trapped in Russian Caucasus tunnel.

text.p: Up to 300 people remained trapped by avalanches in a tunnel in the Caucasus mountains on Monday and it would take at least two more days to rescue them, a spokesman for the Russian Emergencies Ministry said.

Several dozen people and their vehicles were freed on Sunday after being trapped for days inside the four-km (2.5 mile) Roksky tunnel linking Russia's North Ossetia region with the breakaway Georgian province of South Ossetia.
But after rescue workers had cleared away some 19 kilometres (12 miles) of snow blocking the highway, fresh showfalls triggered new avalanches on Monday.
"Strong winds are hampering the evacuation," the Moscow-based ministry spokesman said. "Rescue teams will blow up the snow...and it will take two more days to free the people."
Local authorities planned to use heavy military trucks to try and break through to the trapped people, and set off explosive charges in an attempt to prevent further avalanches.
Itar-Tass news agency said two women had given birth while trapped in the tunnel and one new-born child had died of the cold. Two other people were reported to have died in the area over the weekend.

Rescue teams and doctors, entering the tunnel by foot, have managed to deliver food, medicine and warm clothing. Some of the motorists trapped in it have refused to leave in case their cars are stolen or looted, agencies said.

Georgian leader Eduard Shevardnadze, speaking on national radio, said snowfalls in the mountains and floods in the west of the former Soviet republic were "a natural disaster on a wide scale" which had seriously damaged the economy.
In western Georgia, floods have ruined hunderds of buildings and over 50 bridges, Tass said.

After an unusually warm period lasting to mid-December, a cold snap has hit most of Russia. Tass reported that 10 people had died of cold in the past week and another 245 were taken to hospital suffering from frost-bite.
In the Siberian region of Yakutia, 10,000 reindeer have died of starvation because of ice covering their pastures, the spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry said.
However a spokeswoman for Russia's Methereological Centre said temperatures across the European part of Russia were only a few degrees lower than normal for this time of the year.
She said temperatures were likely to stay at about minus 20- 25 Centigrade (minus 4-13F) at night and minus 10-15 Centigrade (minus 4-5F) during the day up to the New Year.
"We have been spoiled by warm winters for the last five years. Such cold winters are normal for this region," the spokeswoman said.
